relevance_ranking.rubric: Score /100: O2 30*max(0,1-|delta percentage points|/20); P 25*max(0,1-|delta kPa|/60); gravity 15*exp(-|g_environment-0|/0.2); area 5*min(1,area/0.04m2); behavior 5 fabric spread, 4 anchored PMMA, 3 otherwise; data 6 for gas/thermal +4 for published numeric spread; ground-comparison 10 if available. Ties ordered by test_id. Differences smaller than sensor uncertainty are not scientifically significant.

The same atmosphere assumptions for lunar base and rover intentionally yield equal rankings

key_insights.statement: Los 218 archivos contienen nueve pruebas medidas de Saffire-II, identificadas localmente como PSI-99; no aportan seis misiones independientes.
La presión previa medida abarca 102.50–102.76 kPa y el O2 del sensor 21.52–21.80%; la similitud atmosférica favorece los escenarios ISS/Gateway asumidos.
Las bases lunares y marcianas y el rover reciben un ranking de transferencia condicionado: ninguna prueba local valida baja presión, O2 enriquecido o gravedad parcial.
El piloto de nueve pruebas obtiene RMSE LOOCV 23.45 ppm frente a 41.42 ppm de la media de entrenamiento; la selección usa la misma CV y requiere validación externa.
Las dos pruebas SIBAL publican 2.1 y 2.6 mm/s con caudal medido de 19.99 y 24.99 cm/s: un aumento de velocidad de 23.8%, descriptivo con n=2.
El CO2 previo varía entre 3307 y 4334 ppm; restar la línea base local evita confundir acumulación de pruebas previas con la respuesta del ensayo.

Las 4 muestras de silicona no sostuvieron propagación en estas condiciones; sus comparaciones de 1g muestran que material y régimen de gravedad/flujo deben conservarse al interpretar la selección preventiva.
Hay señales de humo de Cygnus, pero faltan umbrales/eventos de alarma y una sincronización verificada; no se informa un tiempo de detección ni un margen seguro para la tripulación.
Faltan O2 de entrada/salida con caudal másico y una intervención documentada de corte de flujo; los datos no dimensionan por sí solos HRR ni eficacia de supresión.

discrepancies: No raw tests from Saffire I, III, IV, V or VI
CO, acid gases, particle mass, alarm thresholds and exposure limits unavailable
No inlet/outlet O2 pair, exhaust mass flow, or validated mixed cabin volume for HRR
Preflight and postflight thicknesses and sample-6 flow disagree
Published O2 is CO2-derived; sensor O2 fluctuates; no atmosphere-response fit is supported
Radiometers have different views of samples; local flux is not total power
Repeated image variants and zero-filled cabin telemetry require filtering
Cygnus and Saffire clocks cannot be assigned per-test reliably from cached alignment columns
assumptions: Nominal specimen geometry follows postflight matrix except preflight 10mm nominal for grooved PMMA
Material inheritance for empty II-6 and II-9 cells and 037-to-0.37 correction are documented
Electrical pulse defines t=0; optical ignition time may differ
One-second medians and fixed windows reduce unequal-cadence and duration effects
CO2 percent to ppm multiplier 10000; PSIA to kPa multiplier 6.894757293168; mW/cm2 to kW/m2 multiplier 0.01
No published numeric spread value is represented as an independently calculated value
Habitat atmospheres are analyst design scenarios

limitations: Nine test records in one flight; no independent flight validation or randomized replicates
Model selected by repeated LOOCV; reported best error has selection optimism
A single PMMA-Nomex composite test cannot validate material-specific generalization
Material, geometry, sample location, flow and ignition energy are confounded
Only two quantitative published spread rates; no independently calibrated optical-front extraction
Sensor offsets and mixing dominate some small CO2 responses; negative changes are not physical CO2 consumption
Uncertainty describes window variability, not absolute sensor accuracy or a confidence interval
No CO, acid gas or particle-mass channels and no applicable exposure/alarm thresholds
Cygnus clock alignment is unverified; mission telemetry cannot be assigned to per-test alarm delays
No HRR from oxygen consumption without paired channels/mass flow or validated cabin mass balance
No controlled ventilation cutoff or extinguishment effectiveness measurements
No enriched-O2/low-pressure or lunar/Martian partial-gravity experiments in this archive
Rankings use illustrative analyst atmosphere assumptions and subjective weights, not mission requirements
Reported damage length, fuel regression, flame tip and pyrolysis propagation are different physical quantities
